title: PR tinker log and micro-refactor checklist
content:
Context:
Quick running log for the pile of small PRs I'm touching this sprint. Goal: make safe, low-risk edits that improve observability and reduce tail latency variance without big integration risk. This is intentionally messy — notes-to-self while I flip between PRs and local runs.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Small, focused changes to logging + metric labels + early-exit guards reduce debugging time 30% and lower alert noise without touching scheduling logic.
- Conservative inlining of KV-cache metrics (per-request keys) gives actionable signal for hot-prefixes; if cost shows up, revert.

Review heuristics (quick):
- No behavioural change without test coverage (unit or integration). If behaviour changed, add opt-in flag and a short deprecation note.
- Change that touches hot path must include microbenchmark numbers (local short-run ok) and a flamegraph snapshot.
- Anything touching cache eviction or KV must include edge-case tests: empty cache, stale entry, concurrent write.

Checklist for each PR I touch (copy to PR description):
- [ ] Summary: one-sentence intent.
- [ ] Risk level: low/medium/high + brief justification.
- [ ] Metrics to monitor post-merge (names and dashboards).
- [ ] Rollout plan: immediate, canary X% for 24h, or staged by region.
- [ ] Revert steps included and validated locally.

Micro-refactor ideas (quick sketches):
1) Split 'request->router->executor' tracing: emit span on router decision with label model_variant (not just model).
   - Why: current traces only show model name; variants hide fallback behavior.
   - Risk: low. Only adds metadata. Add tests that assert span label exists.

2) Lightweight KV cache metrics: per-prefix hit/miss counter + approx entry-size gauge (buckets: small/medium/large).
   - Why: observed noise where token-count spikes but we can't correlate to prefix reuse.
   - Risk: medium (memory instrumentation). Start with sampling 1% of requests.

3) Guard for long-running token streaming: add a watchdog that emits error metric if stream has >N ms gap between chunks.
   - Why: avoids silent stalls that users interpret as 'hang'.
   - Risk: medium/high (could trigger false alarms). Start disabled behind feature flag.

4) Consolidate duplicate helper functions in generation_utils (two helpers with same signature found).
   - Why: small maintenance win.
   - Risk: low. Validate no change in behavior.

Quick testing commands to remember (local):
- run unit: ./scripts/run-tests -k cache* -s
- microbench: ./bench/run_bench --scenario=single-stream --runs=5 --trace=flame.svg
- spinner (simulate slow upstream): python infra/tools/simulate_upstream_delay.py --delay-ms 1500 --path /v1/generate

Follow-ups per PR (example mapping):
- PR #2486 (router tracing): add dashboard tile ‘router:variant rate’ and alert if variant-fallback > 5% for 1h. Owner: Maya.
- PR #2490 (kv metrics sample): run sampling for 48h on staging region eu-west, export results to S3, summary by 2024-02-10. Owner: me.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to tag metrics so cost-accounting team can easily map them to customer ids without PII leakage? (ask Security — Rina).
- Decide default sample rate for KV metrics: 1% seems conservative; is it enough to detect spike patterns?
- Standard format for rollout notes in PR body (copyable template).

Session notes (quick chronology):
- 2024-01-12 09:30: skim PRs; identified 3 low-risk insertion points for labels.
- 2024-01-14 11:00: implemented router label enrichment locally; unit test + microbench run; no perf regression in 5 runs.
- 2024-01-17 16:20: found duplicate helper in generation_utils; extracted common function; added docstring.
- 2024-01-26 14:05: prototyped kv-meter sampling; memory spike on full sampling — keep sampling flag.

Notes-to-self for PR descriptions (short template):
- Summary: "Add router span label for model_variant to improve traceability"
- Risk: low — only emits span metadata; guarded by tests.
- Monitoring: adds metric router.variant.rate and trace annotation; dashboard link.
- Rollout: immediate via canary (10% traffic) for 12h, then full if variant-fallback < 2%.

Potential revert plan (boilerplate):
- Steps: revert PR -> re-deploy -> watch canary dashboards for 30m -> if errors persist, hotfix branch that re-enables previous instrumentation binary.

Rough decision log:
- If KV sampling causes >10% increase in memory/heap RSS in staging, abandon and pivot to aggregated periodic snapshot approach.
- Prefer adding metrics over changing core scheduling heuristics in this sprint.

Slack anchors / refs I want in PR thread:
- #eng-runtime channel, message id: share flamegraph and sampling numbers.
- Mention @Rina for security/metrics tagging guidance.

End-of-day small wins (for checklist):
- router span label: landed in PR branch, awaiting review.
- generation_utils extract: merged to main after tests.
- kv sampling: prototype behind flag; document required rollout cautions.

If I come back to this later:
- Re-run bench with full load profile (simulate burst pattern) before enabling sampling at >1%.
- Add a short how-to in docs/observability for interpreting new variant labels.

Random ephemeral notes (might delete later):
- think about adding "request origin" as sparse label (value cardinality concerns).
- check if we already emit model_variant in other services (search traces).

---
End of log.
